### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/clk/samsung/clk-gs101.c`**
   - **MUX Clocks**: The existing MUX clock definitions for `PERIC1 USI` instances (USI0, USI9, USI10, USI11, USI12, USI13) were changed from `MUX` to `nMUX`, indicating a change in how these clocks are defined.
   - **DIV Clocks**: The DIV clock definitions for the same `PERIC1 USI` instances were modified from `DIV` to `DIV_F`, and the `CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT` flag was added to each of these definitions. This change allows the clock rate to propagate up the clock tree.
   - **GATE Clocks**: The GATE clock definitions for `PERIC1` instances were updated to include the `CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT` flag, allowing the rate change to propagate for these clocks as well.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications made in the `clk-gs101.c` file are interconnected as they all aim to ensure that the clock rate changes for the SPI source clock (IPCLK) are properly propagated through the clock tree. By changing the MUX definitions to `nMUX`, the system indicates that these clocks can now propagate rate changes. The addition of the `CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT` flag in the DIV and GATE clock definitions ensures that when the SPI driver calls `clk_set_rate()`, the changes will affect not only the leaf clock (IPCLK) but also the parent clocks in the hierarchy, thus maintaining the integrity of the clock configuration across the system. This coordinated approach addresses the original issue of the clock rate not being properly propagated, ensuring that all related clocks reflect the correct rate during SPI transfers.

clk: samsung: gs101: propagate PERIC1 USI SPI clock rate
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

When SPI transfer is being prepared, the spi-s3c64xx driver will call
clk_set_rate() to change the rate of SPI source clock (IPCLK). But IPCLK
is a gate (leaf) clock, so it must propagate the rate change up the
clock tree, so that corresponding MUX/DIV clocks can actually change
their values. Add CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT flag to corresponding clocks for
all USI instances in GS101 PERIC1: USI{0, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13}. This change
involves the following clocks:

PERIC1 USI*:

    Clock                              Div range    MUX Selection
    -------------------------------------------------------------------
    gout_peric1_peric1_top0_ipclk_*    -            -
    dout_peric1_usi*_usi               /1..16       -
    mout_peric1_usi*_usi_user          -            {24.5 MHz, 400 MHz}

With input clock of 400 MHz this scheme provides the following IPCLK
rate range, for each USI block:

    PERIC1 USI*:       1.5 MHz ... 400 MHz

Accounting for internal /4 divider in SPI blocks, and because the max
SPI frequency is limited at 50 MHz, it gives us next SPI SCK rates:

    PERIC1 USI_SPI*:   384 KHz ... 49.9 MHz

Which shall be fine for the applications of the SPI bus.

Note that with this we allow the reparenting of the MUX_USIx clocks to
OSCCLK. Each instance of the USI IP has its own MUX_USI clock, thus the
reparenting of a MUX_USI clock corresponds to a single instance of the
USI IP. The datasheet mentions OSCCLK just in the low-power mode
context, but the downstream driver reparents too the MUX_USI clocks to
OSCCLK. Follow the downstream driver and do the same.

Fixes: 2999e786d7e9 ("clk: samsung: gs101: add support for cmu_peric1")

Acked-by: André Draszik <andre.draszik@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: Tudor Ambarus <tudor.ambarus@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240419100915.2168573-3-tudor.ambarus@linaro.org
Signed-off-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzysztof.kozlowski@linaro.org>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that the SPI source clock (IPCLK) is a gate clock, which means that when its rate is changed using `clk_set_rate()`, the change does not propagate up the clock tree to the corresponding MUX and DIV clocks. This results in the MUX and DIV clocks not reflecting the updated clock rate, leading to potential issues during SPI transfers. The lack of the `CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT` flag in the clock definitions prevents the necessary propagation of the rate change.
